<thought>To meet the requirement of a single‑step synthesis from commercially available, inexpensive precursors, the most straightforward transformation is a palladium‑catalyzed Heck coupling. By coupling 4‑iodoanisole (COc1ccc(I)cc1) with 4‑methoxystyrene (COc1ccc(C=C)cc1) we directly obtain the target 4,4'‑dimethoxystilbene (C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2). Both reagents are readily purchasable and their combined cost is well below $150. The retrosynthetic tree therefore has the target molecule as the root, a single reaction node (Heck coupling, template_id = 10234 – a standard aryl‑halide + alkene Heck reaction), and two leaf molecules representing the two starting materials.</thought>
